module.summary: Linux- and ABI-independent bounded generational resource storage with process-local alias bindings with lossless generation-bearing semantic I/O identity.
module.long_description: Composes generational handles into bounded resource identity, reference counting, capability metadata, and deterministic local binding tables.

purpose.primary: Provide bounded stale-safe resource identity and alias lifetime without compatibility-ABI identity.
non_goals: Linux file descriptors, syscall numbers, errno values, RISC-V registers, VFS objects, concurrency
purpose.future_role: Shared substrate directly consumable by QuirkM typed handles and Wasm adapters without Linux identity.

c_pain.summary: C tagged unions rely on conventions for tag/payload agreement.
c_pain.why_c_is_attractive: A direct enum, union, and switch are compact.
c_pain.where_c_degrades: Tag/payload and callback lifetime rules remain informal.

cross_module: A Morphic semantic I/O request carries both resource slot and generation, distinguishing successive generations in the same bounded slot.

repository.guarantee: stale-reference rejection and bounded inline storage

repository.reason: carry complete ResourceRef identity through semantic I/O

agent_contract.summary: Bounded generational resource identity and deterministic process-local alias bindings.
use_when: Need bounded Linux-independent resource identity and alias lifetime.
do_not_use_when: Need dynamically growing storage or synchronized concurrent mutation.
failure_guarantees: Failed resource and binding operations preserve state.
Semantic I/O identity preserves both the resource slot and generation; stale identities remain rejected after slot reuse.

determinism.ordering: Table order, then zero padding, then argv strings and env strings in input order.

known_gaps: Compile-time capacity; generation wrap remains bounded by project 08.
integration_notes: Adapters keep Linux fd and errno outside this module.
Pass semanticIdentity(reference) end-to-end and reconstruct only with referenceFromIdentity; never assume generation 1.
